Referral Note (primary care)

Mr. Dunmore, a 46-year-old construction supervisor, is referred for psychiatric evaluation after routine laboratory work showed abnormal liver function tests. He reports daily alcohol use. His wife has raised concerns about his drinking and how it is affecting home and work. He has no prior psychiatric history or treatment and takes no psychiatric medication. Medical history is notable for hypertension, treated with hydrochlorothiazide. Referred for evaluation of his alcohol use and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Dressed in work clothes; adequately groomed.

Behavior: Alert and cooperative. Mild bilateral hand tremor.

Speech: Normal rate, volume, and tone.

Mood / Affect: Mood euthymic. Affect appropriate.

Thought / Perception: Thought process logical. No evidence of perceptual disturbance.

Cognition / Insight: Alert. Insight limited regarding alcohol use. Judgment impaired.
